scope: Patch confirmed deployment/authentication defects and improve the typed expression editor's native drag-and-drop. Rebuild a new private IIS/Linux archive. Preserve old reports/archive. No live production installation or expansion to multi-tenant access.

findings.AUTH_PATH: Actual isolated raw HTTP returned200 without bearer for /%61pi/config and /api;ignored/config; canonical /api/config returned403. Raw-prefix authorization disagrees with normalized controller routing.
findings.PYTHON_INPUTS: Python can import a locally added shadow module or timestamp/unchecked-hash bytecode before source-only manifest checks. Existing verifier ignores __pycache__ and does not close deployment/bootstrap import directories.
findings.FRESH_TOOLS: A nominally fresh empty runtime can reuse preexisting generated venv/PostgreSQL tools and hooks without fresh provisioning.
findings.SUPERVISOR_OWNER: A second service supervisor can overwrite the launch link and tear down the first supervisor's SQL stack after backend startup failure.
findings.WRITABLE_INSTALL: Group/other-writable installation components permit another principal to substitute verified inputs between checking and execution.
findings.DRAG_IDENTITY: Generic text/plain palette payloads have no local gesture ownership; node drop compares rendered state then reconstructs current-state ownership. Hover accepts everything without typed feedback.

http.routing: Reject noncanonical request paths before dispatch: percent escapes, semicolons, backslash, repeated slash and dot/dot-dot segments. The sole percent-escape exception is uppercase %3A in the existing document identifier segment /api/v1/documents/server%3A<lowercase UUID>; also accept literal server:<lowercase UUID> there for current direct clients. The UUID must have its exact 8-4-4-4-12 hex shape and end at slash or end-of-path. These document routes always require bearer authorization; no other encoded/literal colon position or encoding alias is permitted. Ordinary query strings remain under existing controller rules. No routing alias grants authorization, even with a valid bearer.
http.authority: Default to bearer-required for every nonpublic path, independent of /api prefix. Public resources are only canonical GET/HEAD /, /index.html and flat /assets/ filenames with the shipped Vite-safe ASCII name grammar and approved static extensions. Other methods and resource lookalikes require bearer. Retain exact configured Host/Origin and duplicate-header checks; forwarded headers never grant authority.
http.headers: Apply no-store/referrer/CSP/nosniff protections to rejection responses as well as success. No input, bearer, launch fragment or model content in security-error logs/responses.

deployment.trusted_bootstrap: Invoke deployment setup/service with /usr/bin/python3 -I -B. Their entry guard imports only built-in sys before rejecting non-isolated invocation. Standard library/distribution interpreter and the checksum-protected shipped entry scripts/manifest are trusted bootstrap inputs. Source-load the exact verified setup/bootstrap helper bytes by compile/exec without loading local .pyc. Do not add deployment directories to sys.path before verification.
deployment.executable_inventory: Before any application helper import/process, verify shipped manifest bytes and reject unlisted .py, .pyc, .pyo, native libraries and configuration in all installed application/bootstrap directories, including deploy and the retrieval root; allow only explicitly declared operator instance configuration and generated configuration locations. Reject local application __pycache__ artifacts rather than skipping them. Prevent new application bytecode with -B/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE in helper and managed application Python launches. Managed third-party venv dependencies remain separately TRUSTED from hash-pinned fresh provisioning; do not claim the source manifest proves their runtime semantics.
deployment.fresh: Fresh initialization refuses preexisting generated venv/PostgreSQL build/install directories before running them, and refuses unknown nonempty runtime state. Initialization and service use the same exclusive nonblocking OS lock before any SQL, capability-file or backend action. An initialized store is never reset to bypass a failure.
deployment.ownership: Require the canonical installation and executable/configuration paths to be owned by the service UID or trusted root and not group/other writable; the install root and private runtime must be service-owned. Root-owned sticky temporary ancestors are permitted for isolated tests, but the owned child must remain protected. Instance configuration and runtime authority/lock files are service-owned regular files with private permissions. Reject symlinks. Normalize archive file modes (ordinary0644, required executable0755); directories must not be writable by another principal. Separately trusted managed dependency runtime links are restricted to generated venv bin/python{,3,3.12} resolving to trusted system Python, venv lib64 resolving to its internal lib, and standard PostgreSQL library SONAME links resolving inside its own lib directory; validate owners/modes of links and resolved targets. No arbitrary executable redirect is accepted.
deployment.lifecycle: Acquire and hold the same private deployment flock throughout initialization or service startup/cleanup. A rejected competing launcher performs no SQL start/stop, token write/unlink or backend spawn. Keep the lock file itself; release only after cleanup. Backend termination/reap precedes SQL stop. Preserve cleanup uncertainty and nonzero failure; never delete application ownership journals to force recovery. Only the owning supervisor removes its launch link.
deployment.environment: Deployment subprocesses retain the existing clean fixed environment and no arbitrary JVM options. All PostgreSQL access remains through pinned SQLeanParser, including readiness/migration. Loopback binding, exact HTTPS origin and tunnel Host, bearer scope, advisory-only Tier1 opt-in, DEFAULT durable/solver and disabled pool stay as in the prior deployment contract.
deployment.threat_boundary: Protect against remote path aliases, malformed/external gestures, stale editor events, accidental/extra executable inputs, other OS principals and concurrent supported supervisors. A malicious same-UID operator or root can replace the trust anchor and is out of scope. Manifest checksum is integrity evidence under a trusted transfer, not a digital signature or defense against a replaced manifest. Windows/IIS/SSH, TLS/key provisioning and actual target security/performance acceptance remain separate.

editor.visuals: Organize all23 existing constructors into clearly labeled palette groups. Show formula/relation/reference distinctions with text and symbols; use structured node cards, connector guides and large dashed typed holes. Display the expected slot schema and current type, make source and blocks simultaneously usable, and retain visible declarations, reference choices and binder names. No new Alloy semantics or e-graph rewrites.
editor.gesture: Create a same-editor ephemeral in-memory gesture descriptor and random opaque nonce at dragstart. Store only the nonce in a dedicated custom DataTransfer type; ignore external/generic text payloads. Descriptor binds exact document/base revision/draft/content generation, kind, source or constructor, reference and binder values at start. Drop requires the same active gesture and exact current controller binding; selection-only changes need not invalidate content identity. Invalidate on completion, dragend, Escape or content replacement. Never use bearer authority in drag payloads.
editor.typing: Use the existing construct/replacement/paste/newContradiction logic for hover preparation and atomic final mutation. Evaluate destination-specific scope and retained nominal slot obligations. Distinguish known incompatible, potentially compatible but unresolved, and checked compatible; unresolved is never labeled type-checked. Hover is advisory and never authorizes a later drop. Bound/cache preview for the hovered target/generation/modifier; do not run all512-node candidate transformations on every pixel event.
editor.atomicity: At controller entry, reject stale/foreign bindings, missing destination/source and descendant/self-invalid moves before publication. Recompute the candidate against current content and publish at most one immutable draft transition. Rejection changes only notice/gesture presentation, not module, accepted revision, clipboard, content generation or provenance. Dropping does not save or commit.
editor.accessibility: Maintain click-to-insert, explicit copy/cut/paste/delete, selection, Escape and native text-editing shortcuts. Provide textual hover feedback and polite status announcements without relying on color. Preserve keyboard focus after successful edits and native touch/click alternatives; do not claim touchscreen drag support or full screen-reader acceptance without tests.

proof_first.surface: Finite policy model of default authentication/public exceptions/canonical-route rejection, rejected unverified/bootstrap inputs, exclusive-owner side-effect permissions, fresh provisioning rejection, gesture ownership/current-generation checks, typed-drop rejection and no-mutation witnesses. Prove positive witnesses as well as rejection statements; acceptance/performance remain separate fields.
proof_first.execution: Compile in two fresh Lean4.34.1 directories and compare .olean and axiom inventories; record contract/source hashes and theorem inventory. No sorry or custom axioms. All six requested council seats review exact final contract before production edits.
proof_first.limits: Lean establishes only the encoded policy, not Java/TypeScript/Python/IIS implementation refinement, cryptography, OS race-freedom, semantic completeness or visual usability. Preserve failed candidates and distinguish tested runtime behavior from proofs.

tests: Raw actual HTTP: prior bypasses rejected without/with bearer, GET and mutation-shaped aliases, public assets and normal authenticated API still work, duplicate/hostile Host/Origin/Authorization and forwarded spoofing remain denied. Include actual frontend percent-encoded and direct literal server:UUID document reads/mutations, unauthorized denial and malformed/double-encoded/extra escape rejection.

Poisoned local standard-library shadow and timestamp/unchecked-hash bytecode cannot execute before rejection. Fresh old-tool sentinels never execute. Group-writable/symlink/root-mismatch/private-file tests fail before helpers. Competing supervisor never writes/removes a link or starts/stops the shared stack.

Typed editor regressions: forged/external/malformed/stale gestures, removed targets, reference scope, relation-vs-formula, unknown constraints, selection-only identity, move/copy, Escape and unchanged-state rejection.
Complete relevant Java/frontend/style and deployment tests in isolated builds; all authored Java/JS/TS methods documented and <=30physical lines, encapsulated state.

Real browser/native drag on an isolated initialized app when browser is available: compatible insertion, incompatible rejection, move/copy, cancellation and keyboard alternative; inspect layout at desktop/narrow widths and save truthful screenshots. Missing native drag capability remains explicitly OPEN, not replaced by synthetic DOM events as evidence.

New private deployment archive with checksum/allowlist/mode audit, fresh Linux setup and HTTP restart smoke after security changes. Preserve previous archive and evidence; update current status with exact remaining Windows/accessibility/commercial gates.
